sections.h2: What are game UI/UX design services?
sections.answer: Game UI/UX design services plan how players move through a video game (UX) and design the screens they see and touch (UI), from the HUD to the game website.

sections.h2: Which game screens do our game UI/UX design services cover?
sections.answer: Our game interface design covers 6 parts of a video game that players touch, each drawn in every screen state: default, loading, error, empty, locked and reward.

items.title: Heads-up display (HUD).
items.body: Health, speed, map and timers stay readable at a glance during motion. Video game UI design services for the HUD add motion and feedback, the core of our interaction design agency work.

items.title: Menus and settings.
items.body: Main menu, pause, controls remapping, audio and subtitle settings, so players find the options they expect without digging through nested menus.

items.title: First-time user experience (FTUE).
items.body: The first session, from launch to the first win, teaches controls inside gameplay instead of a wall of tutorial text.

items.title: Inventory and garage screens.
items.body: Players compare, upgrade and equip items, as in the 3D garage we designed, where Nitro players inspect, upgrade and show off their race cars.

items.title: In-game store.
items.body: Currencies, bundles and the battle pass get clear prices, and every loot box shows its odds before purchase, as Apple and Google Play require.

items.title: Game website and marketplace.
items.body: Roadmap and whitepaper pages explain non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and lead players and investors into the NFT marketplace, built on our UI UX web design practice.

sections.h2: What makes UX design for games different from app UX?
sections.answer: UI UX design for games keeps the intended challenge fun for players and removes friction everywhere else, so they struggle with the game, not the interface.

items.title: Intended challenge vs interface friction
items.body: A hard race is the game working; a hidden settings menu is a defect. Playtesting separates the two by watching where players fail and asking why.

items.title: Readability in motion
items.body: HUD text and icons need contrast and size that hold at speed, so players read health or position at a glance without looking away from the action.

items.title: Input variety
items.body: Mobile game UI design sizes touch targets for thumbs: 44×44 pt on iOS and 48×48 dp on Android, as in our mobile app UI UX design services. Mobile game UX design keeps key actions in thumb reach and plans controller support.

items.title: Trust in the game economy
items.body: Prices, currencies and play-to-earn (P2E) rewards must be clear enough for players and investors to believe. Nitro came to us when investors doubted crypto products, so the racing experience had to earn trust.

sections.h2: What did game UI/UX design deliver for Nitro League?
sections.answer: Our video game UX design shaped the racing game, 3D garage and NFT marketplace website for Nitro League players, and the project secured $5M in funding within 3 months.

Its scope: "idea to product, conceptualisation, art direction, sketching and modeling, MVP launch plan, game and website design, and post-launch enhancements." Discovery and stakeholder interviews led to user flows and a whitepaper; professional gamers validated the result. Read the Nitro League case study.

sections.h2: How does our game UI/UX design process work?
sections.answer: Our game UI/UX design process takes a game studio from discovery to engine-ready handoff in 8–16 weeks (40–80 working days) and 5 steps, with the first designs in 1–2 weeks.

items.title: Discovery and product strategy (5–10 days)
items.body: Stakeholder interviews set the core loop, target audiences and success metrics. Our guide shows what a discovery phase settles before screens.

items.title: User research (5–15 days)
items.body: Designers interview target players and review competitor games to find where onboarding, menus and purchases lose them.

items.title: Information architecture and flows (5–10 days)
items.body: The team maps the menus, the FTUE flow and the purchase flow before any screen is drawn.

items.title: Prototype and validation (10–20 days)
items.body: Five players per round playtest a clickable Figma prototype, the way our usability testing services run sessions, so friction surfaces before engine work starts.

items.title: UI design and handoff (15–25 days)
items.body: Designers finish the HUD and every screen state, then hand Figma specs and sliced UI assets to the Unity engine or Unreal Engine team, with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA on web surfaces.

sections.h2: Game UI/UX design vs game art production
sections.answer: Game UI/UX design decides what players need on each screen and in what order; game art production makes the characters, environments and effects. Hiring a game UI/UX design company instead of a pure art studio fits when players struggle with flows, not visuals. The table compares both disciplines.

sections.h2: How much do game UI/UX design services cost?
sections.answer: Game UI/UX design services cost a game studio $60,000–$180,000 over 8–16 weeks for a full product, or $25,000–$60,000 over 4–8 weeks for a UI sprint on 1–2 surfaces.
sections.body: A full engagement uses 3–6 designers and covers game UI, website and game marketplace; a sprint uses 2–4. Price follows the number of screens and states, target platforms (iOS, Android and web), playtest rounds and website scope. A live game with weak in-game store or FTUE conversion starts with an audit of the live game: $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks via our UX audit services.

sections.h2: Which platform and accessibility standards shape game UI?
sections.answer: Five platform and accessibility standards shape game UI design services for mobile and web games, and each one changes what players see on screen:
items: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: the designing-for-games and game controls pages cover touch controls and game controller support, so on-screen controls are planned per device.

App Store Review Guidelines 3.1.1: apps offering a loot box or other randomized virtual items for purchase must disclose the odds of receiving each type of item before purchase, so the in-game store shows odds on the offer screen.
Google Play payments policy: games that sell randomized virtual items must clearly disclose the odds of receiving them in advance of purchase.
Xbox Accessibility Guidelines and the Game Accessibility Guidelines: both cover subtitles and control remapping, so settings menus offer readable subtitles and remappable controls.
WCAG 2.2 level AA: the game website and NFT marketplace need keyboard access, visible focus and 4.5:1 text contrast.

sections.h2: FAQs about game UI/UX design services
sections.answer: These answers cover the 5 questions a game studio asks most before buying game UI/UX services.

faqs.q: Do you build the game UI in Unity or Unreal Engine?
faqs.a: No. Our designers deliver Figma screens, specs and sliced UI assets, and the game studio's Unity engine or Unreal Engine developers build them. The specs list every screen state, so developers do not have to guess how a locked or reward screen looks.

faqs.q: Can you redesign the UI of a game that is already live?
faqs.a: Yes. Start with an audit of the live game, $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks, that reviews the in-game store, FTUE and menu flows against player reviews and analytics. Its prioritized findings then scope a UI sprint.

faqs.q: Is game UI design outsourcing possible for only the HUD and menus?
faqs.a: Yes. A UI sprint of $25,000–$60,000 over 4–8 weeks covers 1–2 surfaces, for example the HUD and menus, and ends with a playtested prototype. Game UX design outsourcing works the same way: research, flows and playtests come to us while the game studio keeps engine implementation in-house.

faqs.q: Do you design mobile game UI for iOS and Android?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile game UI design follows the Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Google Play policies, with touch targets of 44×44 pt on iOS and 48×48 dp on Android. The game website around the app follows WCAG 2.2 level AA.

faqs.q: Have you designed a web3 or play-to-earn game?
faqs.a: Yes. Nitro League is a play-to-earn racing game with an NFT marketplace, a 3D garage, and tokenomics and IDO (initial decentralized exchange offering) launch screens; its platform also includes a metaverse where users buy and sell properties, production factories and garages.
